text:
maria: quick sync - scenario: eu region forced eviction, traffic fails over to us. legal reminder: certain tenants (eu-pii) must never have inference executed outside eu. how do we guarantee that under active/active failover?
ken: fail-closed for eu-pii tenants. no execution outside eu. we can surface degradation but not execute.
devon: implementation options: warm standby in eu, reserved dedicated pool for residency tenants, immediate 503 for blocked tenants, or transparent proxying to a customer-managed in-region endpoint.
ashley: ops callout: eu builds are int8-q, us builds int4-q. aside from numeric drift, the main blocker is cross-border execution. also, cache hydration is risky.
jon: proposal: edge proxy enforces residency policy. pseudocode: ```if tenant.tags contains 'eu-pii' and request.region != 'eu': return 503, 'residency_blocked' else route as normal``` Means we must carry tenant residency info in auth token and evaluate before model selection.
maria: is an app-visible 503 acceptable? product said for high-sensitivity customers some SLA tiers accept degraded availability, but we need per-tenant controls.
ken: agree. default policy: untagged tenants -> best-effort; residency-tagged -> fail-closed. minimal blast radius.
devon: cache/kv semantics: never hydrate residency-tagged keys into foreign-region caches. three behaviors for a cache miss from a foreign region: (1) proxy-fetch from origin region (no data at rest in foreign cache), (2) return miss and let app degrade, (3) reject upfront. which is legal-safe?
ashley: legal quick check: cross-region reads of ephemeral inputs are only allowed if explicitly pseudonymized or consented. assume deny-by-default. so proxy-fetch is risky unless tenant opted-in.
jon: propose adding: tenant.residency_mode = [strict, allow-cross-read, allow-cross-exec]; default strict for enterprise PII. Console exposes this flag to tenant admins.
maria: good. also need telemetry: counts of blocked execs, blocked cache hydra, and proxy-fetched reads (if allowed). dashboards must show rejected_eu_pii_count and routed_best_effort_count.
ken: i'll add metrics: residency.exec_blocked, residency.cache_blocked, residency.cache_proxy_fetch. include trace tag residency.enforced=true + tenant_id_hash for audits.
ops-bot: chaos-svc: EU eviction exercise scheduled tommorow 09:00 UTC. tagging test-run with residency=true. @ken @devon @ashley
devon: for the canary: simulate EU outage and assert that requests for tenants with tag "eu-pii" return 503 and produce residency.exec_blocked logs. other tenants should route to best-effort fallback.
ashley: runbooks: update failover checklist to include: 1) ensure residency flag propagation 2) confirm no cache hydration of residency keys 3) monitor residency.exec_blocked metric 4) manual unblock flow if customer has emergency consent.
jon: follow-up RFC I'll draft: residency enforcement at proxy, cache-tagging rules, tenant.residency_mode enum, console controls, metrics, and operator unblock flow. link in thread when draft is ready.
maria: action items: jon -> RFC draft; devon -> small PR for proxy short-circuit + unit tests; ken -> metrics + chaos canary; ashley -> runbook update & legal confirmation on cache-read exceptions. please confirm by EOD.
ken: confirmed. aiming for PR + canary by EOD. :thumbsup:
jon: RFC link (draft): https://rfc.internal/r/986-residency-guardrails (DRAFT) - please comment.
maria: thanks. reminder: we must also ensure rollout is gradual and observable. during chaos do not auto-unblock tenants. manual operator path only.
ops-bot: reminder: incident playbook 'region-failover' v2.1 will be used for the exercise. chaos run tags: residency=true, high-sensitivity=on.
